text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- NATO summit has invited Poland, Hungary and the Czech republic to join the treaty which means which extends the Euroatlantic security area eastward by 500 kilometres.

- Poland's Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek is dissatisfied with the recent round of trade talks with Russia which finished in Moscow yesterday. Current misunderstandings between the two countries with regard to trade relations are a result of Poland's foreign policy in the years 1991-1993, Kaczmarek said. He expressed his favour for what he called a strategic alliance between the two countries' arms industries.

- Heavy rainfalls in the last few days resulted in the malfunction of 16,000 telephones in east Warsaw. Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) the state-owned telecoms operator has guaranteed to repair the system by July 15, TPSA said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Era GSM digital mobile phone operator has signed a roaming agreement with the US Omnipoint PCS-1900 operator. Era's subscribers will be allowed to use their SIM access cards in telephone equipment hired in America and the same will apply to Omnipoint's US customers visiting Poland, Era said.
- Germany's Pfeifer und Langen sugar concern plans to buy controlling stakes in four sugar mills controlled by the Poznansko-Pomorska Spolka Cukrowa (PPSC) sugar group in western Poland.
- Trading on the Warsaw bourse in the first half of 1997 grew by 86 percent compared with the same period last year, the bourse said.
- The BDM PKO SA brokerage house will launch the PKO/Credit Suisse investment trust units priced at 50 zlotys per unit today.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Poland's finance ministry has opposed the VAT tax write-offs by companies buying vehicles of up to 500 kg loading capacity demanded by a group of parliamentary deputies.

- The privatisation of the PZU insurance firm will most likely start by the end of July. The cabinet's economic ministers' committee (KERM) approved the plan of capital restructuring of the firm proposed by PZU's president Jan Monkiewicz last week.

- The Budopol Wroclaw construction firm in south-western Poland plans an issue of up to 1,500 000 shares in a public offering to up share capital by four million zlotys, the Penetrator monthly said. Budopol Wroclaw is controlled by the listed Mostostal Export.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Alima Gerber baby food maker and trader in Rzeszow, south-eastern Poland, which is controlled by the international Novartis concern, has opened its representative office in Moscow. "Russia's market for our products is sure to develop and there is still no real competition there", Alima-Gerber's official Daniel Kortlan said.
- Ukraine's Zaporozhec automotive plant plans to produce 150,000 engines every year for the Korean Daewoo cars made in Poland, Zaporozhec's president Oleksander Sotnikov said.

- The listed Agros' fruit and vegetable processing group has bought the Korporacja Rolna dairy, distillery and farming complex worth 17 million zlotys. Agros guaranteed to invest 12 million zlotys in development in the next five years.
PARKIET

- Poland's treasury ministry will shortly announce the full list of investors interested in buying the Polfa Poznan and Polfa Stargard Gdanski pharmaceutical plant as the tender deadline expires today.
